newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes sink with NYMEX, ANS quiet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes sink with NYMEX, ANS quiet.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes tracked sinking prices for oil and refined product futures early Tuesday, but interest in spot Alaskan crude remained faint because local refiners felt squeezed by margins.
"It's very quiet," said a seller of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude.
Buyers hoped the drop in NYMEX prices would lower ANS to reasonable levels. January crude fell 82 cents to $24.48 a barrel at 1152 PST.
Rises in crude futures, and static product values, have forced buyers to pay up and kept ANS trade thin.
Players in the ANS spot market failed to strike deals early Tuesday and sellers reported few inquiries.

The ANS discount was flat at $1.75 under cash January barrels of West Texas Intermediate, which pressured ANS by falling 50 cents in the early afternoon to $24.60/24.70 a barrel. WTI fell another 25 cents near the close of NYMEX.
Outright ANS prices reacted by falling to $22.80/23 a barrel.
Traders said a local trading house offered Koch Alberta, a ANS substitute, but no buyers came forward.
Offers for Alaskan crude stayed $1.65 under WTI while buyers kept bids at $2.00 under.

Dealers said 12,000 bpd term deal of Argentine Rincon crude remained unsold in the spot market. Unocal last week bought 12,000 bpd of Rincon under a four month term deal. The deal is set at 90 cents off February WTI and will last four months.
Recent Line 63 deals were done on a posting plus basis only, traders said, with premiums talked $0.95 to $1.05 in the thinly traded market.
Line 63 at a discount to WTI had not been seen in months, traders said, noting deals done in the posting plus market fell between $0.95 abd $1.05.
Meanwhile, problems at several California refineries left an excess of local heavy grades in spot markets, traders said.
Mobil and Texaco had excess following fires late last month, and Chevron's plant near San Francisco remained reduced on talks of a fire late last week.
Discounts for Kern River heavy crude remained 10 cents under postings to even with postings, traders said.
Outright prices increased 30 cents to $18.00/18.10 a barrel after more oil companies reported posted price increases Monday.
Wilmington premiums stagnated at 55 to 65 cents over postings, but outright prices rose 20 cents on the increased postings.
